opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; Engineers own Source Code (admin allowed), but requested write is at/below the maximum. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 (Dominic Taylor) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes about E004 conflict on employment type: one says full_time Engineer (recommend write), the other says contractor with basic security training (recommend read). Under contractor policy, write is only permitted with advanced security training; with basic training the maximum is read. Since the requested write level exceeds the maximum under the contractor classification, and granting write would violate policy if that classification is correct, I grant the safer maximum of read.
